newsitem.title: FRANCE: Goldsmith's EDN to announce revival on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Goldsmith's EDN to announce revival on Friday.

text.p: The defunct Europe of Nations (EDN) group in the European Parliament, led by British billionaire James Goldsmith, is expected to announce its revival on Friday, an EDN official said on Tuesday.
The official confirmed that only one Euro-MP was expected to join the former members of the anti-federalist EDN and reconstitute the group.
He said the announcement would be made in the country of the Euro-MP concerned but declined to say where that would be.

Parliament sources told Reuters last week the most likely candidate was Hans Kronberger, a Euro- MP elected on October 13 from the list put up by Joerg Haidar's far-right Austrian Freedom Party (FPO).
They cited two other FPO members, Peter Sichrovsky and Klaus Lukas, British Conservative James Nicholson and Dutch Christian Democrat James Janssen van Raay as possible new EDN members.
The EDN collapsed in November following the defection to the Christian Democrat European People's Party (EPP) of Anne Christine Poisson, one of its French members.
Poisson's departure left the EDN with 17 members -- one short of the minimum needed to form a group.
After weeks of rumours in and around Parliament that the EDN was wooing Haidar's FPO to stave off collapse, the EDN in October issued a statement denying all contacts with "extremists".
When the party officially collapsed in November, the former EDN Euro-MPs found themselves relegated to the non-aligned benches.
Kronberger, Sichrovsky and Lukas were elected on the platform put up by the FPO but were not actually members of the Freedom Party, one Parliament source said.
